rubric_items.reason: Every S-n/ACm has a test. TP-21 now covers S-4/AC4. S-3/AC4 is still only partly tested: TP-12 uses 14 Nov and never compares the 16 Nov 'Not available' schedule with picking that date by hand.

API rules and write-route responses are integration tests with Supertest. Rendering and ?date= handling are unit tests with Testing Library. No e2e tests are planned. Each check sits at the cheapest level that proves it.

Negative tests now cover the field on PATCH (TP-19) and POST (TP-22), entry keys and the 404 (TP-20), and invalid ?date= (TP-14). The PUT response is tested for recomputation (TP-23). Boundaries include UTC vs local midnight, free 0 and all-passed days.
Tools and the web test file match the strategy and layout. Test titles still start with 'API:'/'Web:' instead of a requirement ID, against the rule the plan cites (C3). No API test file is named.

Titles are concrete and runnable, and the 'not echoed' and 'validDay' wording is fixed. Several covers mappings name criteria the test does not exercise (TP-20, TP-22, TP-23), which makes it harder to read what is covered.

findings.text: Still open from attempt 1 (F-3): the plan says every test name starts with its HMS-9 requirement ID, but every title starts with 'API:'/'Web:'. Existing tests use names like 'HMS-7 REQ-8: ...'.

cites.quote: Every test name starts with its HMS-9 requirement ID (C3).
API: at 2026-11-11T19:00Z (00:30 on 12 Nov IST) nextSevenDays dates are 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-18
HMS-7 REQ-8: the other sections are still shown

findings.suggested_fix: Start each TP title with 'HMS-9 REQ-n:' taken from the story trace, for example 'HMS-9 REQ-2: ...'.

findings.text: Still open from attempt 1 (F-4): TP-12 now claims S-3/AC4 but only checks that ?date=2026-11-14 sets the date. Nothing checks that the 16 Nov 'Not available' schedule matches what it shows when 16 Nov is picked by hand.

cites.quote: shows exactly what it shows today when 16 Nov is picked by hand
Web: opening /doctors/:id?date=2026-11-14 sets the day schedule date to 2026-11-14

findings.suggested_fix: Add a check that opens ?date=2026-11-16 for a day with no availability and compares the schedule with picking 16 Nov by hand.

findings.text: Still open from attempt 1 (F-5), and now wider. TP-20, TP-22 and TP-23 are API tests mapped to S-4/AC2 (other page sections unchanged), and TP-23 is also mapped to S-2/AC1 (the page shows 'Not available'). These tests do not exercise those criteria.

cites.quote: then every section other than 'Next 7 days' shows the same content as on the build before this change

findings.suggested_fix: Trace the write-route and entry-key tests to the design endpoints (EP-1, EP-3 to EP-5) and REQ-10, not to page-level story criteria.

findings.text: The design keeps the day schedule's date in sync when the URL's date changes on the same page, for example when a row is clicked. TP-11 checks only the href, and TP-12 checks only the initial load, so the in-page update is untested.

cites.quote: keeps the date state in sync when the URL's `date` changes (for example, when a row is clicked on the same page)
Web: each date links to /doctors/:id?date=YYYY-MM-DD, including a 'Not available' day

findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that clicks a row on the rendered page and checks that the day schedule date changes to that row's date.

cites.quote: API tests use Vitest and Supertest against a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with a fixed clock.
Vitest with jsdom and Testing Library.
Every PRD requirement has at least one test whose name starts with its ID
no page is tested end to end in a browser
The new field is named `nextSevenDays` and holds one entry per day with date, available, booked and free.
HMS-7 set the precedent that `the read-only count in a PATCH body is ignored`
The day link uses a `?date=` parameter on the doctor page.
DoctorService.create ends with `return this.get(id);`, so the POST response is the doctor detail.
DoctorService.replaceAvailability ends with `return this.get(id);`, so the availability PUT response is the doctor detail.
